summary: Redwood hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for Aurora Legal's search relevance use case. Walkthrough included API samples, console demo, Optimize recommendations, and security/QoS discussion. Customer interested in a short hosted pilot pending security docs and performance numbers.
topics: Console demo: model selection, monitoring, cost breakdown
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, data retention
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir Patel from Redwood, AE on the account, with Lina Ortiz our Solutions Engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: Doing well, thanks. Busy week but excited to see this.
[00:12] Daniel: Hi, Samir, Lina. Daniel here. We're particularly focused on improving our search relevance for legal docs - lots of long form text, precedents, and metadata.
[00:23] Samir: Great, that aligns well. Quick agenda - we'll run a hosted API demo for embeddings and our rerank endpoint, show the console for monitoring and Optimize suggestions, then leave time for security and next steps.
[00:36] Lina: I'll start with the API flow - show how you get embeddings for documents, do nearest neighbor, then call our rerank endpoint to rescore results with context.
[00:44] Maya: Sounds good. A couple things for context: we currently use Elastic + a lightweight vector plugin for similarity; we saw issues with precision on multi-paragraph queries. Cost is a concern and also PII retention rules.
[00:58] Samir: Totally - we'll highlight retention controls and KMS options. Also, when you say precision on multi-paragraph, can you give an example?
[01:07] Maya: Sure - a user will paste a 2-3 paragraph brief and expect hits that consider the whole brief, not just phrase match.
[01:15] Lina: That's where embeddings + rerank shine. You do a coarse search via vector similarity, then the rerank endpoint takes the query and candidate docs and scores them with a context-aware model.
[01:26] [01:30] Lina: Ok demo time - hitting the embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with doc text, returns 1536-d vector. (note: numbers rounded in demo)
[01:38] Samir: We also provide batch endpoints for embeddings to reduce per-request overhead.
[01:44] [02:00] Lina: Now I'll show a simple rerank call - you send the query plus top N candidates (id + snippet) and we return a score and optional explanation. The payload is small; examples in the workshop repo.
[02:18] Daniel: How does this compare latency-wise? We're sensitive to tail latency.
[02:24] Lina: For hosted API, typical rerank latencies are 40-120ms depending on model and sequence length. For long context (several KB), expect higher, we can quantify in the benchmark.
[02:38] Maya: And cost? Because reranking per query could be expensive if we send 50 candidates.
[02:44] Samir: Good point - in practice teams do coarse vector search at 0.5-2ms with a vector DB, then rerank top 5-10 candidates. Our Optimize product recommends candidate counts and batching to balance cost and precision.
[02:57] [03:10] Lina: I'm pulling up the Console - model catalog shows 'embed-4096' and two rerank model tiers. You can pin a model for the route, enable streaming, and set a fallback policy to a cheaper model if latency spikes.
[03:24] Maya: Can you show the cost breakdown?
[03:27] Lina: Sure - per-route cost chart, tokens -> USD, plus embedding unit costs. We also show token distribution and top-k latencies.
[03:36] [03:40] Samir: For Aurora Legal, we'd recommend starting with our mid-tier rerank model and 8-candidate rerank, run quality evals on a sample set.
[03:49] Daniel: What's the onboarding time? We have procurement and security gates.
[03:54] Samir: Self-serve onboarding is minutes, but ramping to production with SSO, network controls, and a pilot usually takes 2-4 weeks. For enterprise we can enable a dedicated capacity or private deployment later.
[04:07] Priya: On the security side - SOC2 is a baseline. We need details on data retention, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS key ownership, and audit logs. Also SCIM/SSO integration.
[04:19] Samir: Absolutely - we'll send SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integration in Dedicated/Private; hosted has encrypted at rest with customer key options via bring-your-own-key for some plans. Audit logs and per-request metadata available in the Console.
[04:34] [05:00] Lina: Back to the rerank specifics: we do two-stage scoring - embed similarity first, then rerank with the full model that conditions on the query + doc snippet. The rerank response includes a numeric score and an explain string sometimes - note that the explain is heuristic and not deterministic.
[05:18] Maya: Do you store query text by default?
[05:22] Samir: By default we retain logs for 30 days for troubleshooting; retention is configurable. For the pilot, we can set retention to 7 days or disable logging entirely.
[05:32] Daniel: We will need a data processing agreement and guaranteed deletion policy.
[05:36] Samir: We'll include that in the contract.
[05:40] [06:00] Lina: Now a live example - I send a 3-paragraph legal brief as the query, we run vector similarity, I show top 10 candidates, then call rerank. You'll see ordering change and an increased relevance score for precedent that covers the full brief.
[06:18] [06:30] Lina: (typing) ok sent - here's the response, top candidate moved from position 4 to position 1 after rerank. Scores are normalized 0-1 in the response.
[06:40] Maya: Nice. There are some quirks with multi-paragraph synonyms - do you support custom fine-tuning or just prompts?
[06:47] Lina: Hosted models don't support customer fine-tuning but we support prompt templates, conditioning, and model variants. For very specific corpora we recommend Dedicated with model-adaptation options or running private infra with a tuned model.
[07:00] Samir: Also Optimize can suggest quantization or a smaller rerank model if cost is a bigger constraint. It looks at token distribution and suggests batching sizes.
[07:10] [07:30] Daniel: Can you explain caching - you mentioned KV cache earlier? In our notes we saw 'k v cash' in transcript from a previous demo, haha.
[07:38] Lina: (laugh) yeah transcription loved that. We mean KV cache - we cache key/value attention states for autoregressive workloads; for embeddings/rerank workloads we use prefix caching and result caching. That can reduce repeated work for identical queries.
[07:53] Maya: For search, many queries are near-duplicates. Would caching actually help?
[07:58] Lina: It helps for identical or highly-similar queries; Optimize will profile and recommend caching rules; plus you can implement your own LRU cache on the vector DB side.
[08:10] [08:30] Priya: For compliance, does Redwood support private deployments or VPC peering?
[08:35] Samir: Yes - Dedicated capacity provides reserved GPU pools and VPC peering; Private on-prem option exists for strict data residency. We'll put customer-managed KMS and HSM options in the security pack.
[08:47] Priya: Logs for audit - can we stream to our SIEM?
[08:51] Lina: Yes, audit logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint or S3; we also support syslog/HTTP forwarders.
[08:59] [09:10] Daniel: Back to evaluation - what metrics should we look at for A/B? Precision@k? nDCG?
[09:16] Lina: Precision@k and nDCG are common. We normally run a human-labeled eval set and show delta in nDCG and also track latency and cost per query.
[09:29] Maya: We have a dataset of around 2000 queries with expected relevance. We'll share that.
[09:34] Samir: Perfect. We'll run the benchmark and return a spreadsheet with nDCG deltas and cost numbers.
[09:40] [10:00] Lina: Quick note on model choices - for legal text, we often recommend models with longer context windows to capture paragraphs; sequence length impacts both latency and cost.
[10:12] Daniel: How does rerank handle metadata fields like statute tags or jurisdiction?
[10:17] Lina: You can include metadata as structured fields in the candidate snippets; we also support function/tool calling patterns where metadata is passed as separate fields and the reranker conditions on them. Sometimes we prepend jurisdiction tokens to the query.
[10:32] Maya: Any concerns about PII? We have redactions for client names.
[10:37] Samir: You can pre-redact PII on your side before sending. For the pilot we can set up a redaction pipeline. Hosted offers optional content-filtering.
[10:48] [11:00] Priya: What's the SLA on hosted?
[11:03] Samir: Hosted is best-effort for small accounts. For guaranteed SLOs we do Dedicated with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets.
[11:11] Daniel: We expect spikes during brief uploads. Auto-scaling?
[11:15] Lina: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Hosted has managed autoscaling but without reserved capacity guarantees.
[11:25] [12:00] Lina: Ok demo wrap - I showed embeddings batch, rerank call, console cost/latency, and Optimize suggestions.
[12:08] Maya: That was helpful. A few nitty details on pilot: can the pilot route traffic to a cheaper fallback model if we hit budget caps?
[12:16] Samir: Yes - in the route config you can set fallback to a lower-cost model and even set a hard budget cap alert.
[12:24] [12:30] Daniel: Procurement will want an MSA and DPA; is there boilerplate we can start with?
[12:34] Samir: We'll attach our standard MSA/DPA with the pilot docs.
[12:38] Priya: On keys, our security team prefers BYOK. Is that possible on hosted?
[12:44] Samir: BYOK is supported for some enterprise plans and definitely on Dedicated/Private. We'll clarify for the pilot.
[12:52] [13:10] Lina: I'll note down the technical follow-ups: sample logs, benchmark run, traffic profile.
[13:17] Maya: One last question - do you have references for legal customers?
[13:21] Samir: We can share anonymized case studies; I'll include a short list.
[13:27] [14:00] Samir: Ok let's recap actions and timeline: we'll send security docs and pricing by Tue the 13th, Lina will share benchmark templates by Wed the 14th, customer to share logs by Fri the 15th, and we aim to kick off the pilot the week of the 18th.
[14:18] Daniel: That works.
[14:22] Maya: Thanks, very productive.
[14:25] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the demo repo, benchmark sheet, and meeting notes.
[14:33] [14:40] (call ends)

Notes / links referenced: "Benchmark spreadsheet" (link: shared internally), "Security whitepaper + SOC2" (will be attached), demo repo with sample rerank payloads (link: https://github.com/redwood/demo-rerank).

Transcription artifacts / errors to be aware of: occasional mis-hearing of 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' or 'k v cash'; some proper nouns may be mangled (e.g., model names in the transcript are illustrative).
